# Q1. Loading the data

```{r}

# Your student number goes here
ysn = 1895211
# Calculate your student number modulo 3
filenum <- ysn %% 3
filenum
filename <- paste0("./data/archery_",filenum,".csv")
filename

# Read in the data
tibble_data <- read_csv(filename, na= c("NA", "XX"))
head(n=10, tibble_data)
# Display the first 10 lines of the data
```

# Q2. Taking a random sample of archers

```{r}
#
set.seed(ysn)
sample_archers <-sample_n(tibble_data, 100, replace = FALSE)
head(n=10, sample_archers)
```


# Q3. Tidying the data

## Q3(a). Converting from wide form to long form
```{r}
#

tidying_the_data <- gather(sample_archers, key = "session", value = "result", session_1:session_6)
```

## Q3(b). Replacing `result` with 2 new columns
```{r}
#
tidying_the_data <-tidying_the_data %>%
mutate(
  shots = str_match(result, "(\\d+)shots")[,2],
  hits = str_match(result, "(\\d+)times")[,2]
 )  %>% relocate("shots", .before = result) %>%
  relocate("hits", .before = result) %>% select(name:hits)
```

## Q3(c). Replace data in `session` column with session number
```{r}
#
tidying_the_data <- tidying_the_data %>%
  mutate(session = str_match(session, "session_(\\d+)")[,2])

```

## Q3(d). Replace "Yes/No" with "TRUE/FALSE"
```{r}
#
tidying_the_data <- tidying_the_data %>%
  mutate(experienced = fct_recode(tidying_the_data$experienced, "FALSE"="No", "TRUE"="Yes"))
head(n=10, tidying_the_data)

```

# Q4. Identifying data types

Name - This is a Categorical nominal variable because it's just a label used to identify someone, it does not show any ranking.

Experienced - this data is Categorical nominal variable as it  has only 2 categories True and False  where order or ranking does not matter.

Started - This data has dates in it so this is a quantitative continuous variable as time can't be categorized like nominal or ordinal, time keeps going on without any breaks.

Session - This variable type is Categorical ordinal as it can be put in a order or ranking.

Shots - Shots can be considered as quantitative discrete variable as they are unique to every archer which makes it discrete
Hits- This can also be considered as quantitative discrete variable because it records all the different hits made by different archers making it a discrete value

# Q5. Taming the data
```{r}
#
tidying_the_data$shots <- as.integer(tidying_the_data$shots)
tidying_the_data$hits <- as.integer(tidying_the_data$hits)
tidying_the_data$session <- as.ordered(tidying_the_data$session)
tidying_the_data$started <- dmy(tidying_the_data$started)
head(n=10, tidying_the_data)

```

# Q5.b) Confirming the remaining varaiables to the "tame data" conventions
```{r}
#
tidying_the_data <- tidying_the_data %>% mutate(started = dmy(tidying_the_data$started))
tidying_the_data <- tidying_the_data%>%mutate(session=as.ordered(tidying_the_data$session))
head(n=10, tidying_the_data)
```


# Q6. Adding two new columns to the tidy dataset
```{r}
tidying_the_data$days_experience <- dmy('01/02/2024') - tidying_the_data$started
tidying_the_data$accuracy <- tidying_the_data$hits/tidying_the_data$shots
head(n=10,tidying_the_data)
```
# Q7. displaying the sample statistics for the numerical value in the dataset
```{r}
inspect_num(tibble_data)
```


#Q.8 Data set of expereinced archers
```{r}

data_filtered <- tidying_the_data %>% filter(experienced == TRUE)
head(data_filtered, n = 10)

```
# Q9. Graph who can practice shooting the best
```{r}

ggplot(data_filtered, aes(x = days_experience, y = accuracy)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth()
```
